raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59998. On non-SM100 GPUs, declare the five KV cache layouts FlashInfer can address, so layout resolution can no longer pick LHBNC.

### User case

1. FlashInfer on SM80/SM90/SM120 with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`.
2. `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()` returns `None` there, so `resolve_kv_cache_layout` accepts LHBNC.
3. FlashInfer only takes NHD/HND pages; `get_flashinfer_layout_string` has no LHBNC entry.
4. The engine dies at startup on `AssertionError: KV cache layout LHBNC has no FlashInfer equivalent` (A100, Llama-3-8B) instead of rejecting the layout at resolution.

The fix returns the default preference order without LHBNC (LBNHC, LBHNC, BLNHC, BLHNC, BHLNC) instead of `None`.

Unchanged: the default layout (still LBNHC), the SM100 set, connector preferences (LBHNC and BLHNC stay valid), and every layout FlashInfer could already run.

Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR covers this. #46329 and #56550 add an SM120 branch to the same function but keep the `None` fallback. Related: #55431, #55312.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py \
  -k test_flashinfer_declares_only_layouts_it_can_address
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py
git diff --check
```

The new test patches the device capability to SM80/90/100/120 and checks that every declared layout maps through `get_flashinfer_layout_string` and that LHBNC is not declared.

## Test Result

```text
4 passed; on main 3 fail (SM80/90/120: supported_kv_cache_layouts() is None)
ruff check, ruff format --check (v0.14.0), git diff --check: passed
```

| A100, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, FlashInfer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` | `AssertionError` during startup | `ValueError` at resolution listing the 5 valid layouts |
| default | LBNHC, serves | LBNHC, serves |

<details>
<summary>Test environment</summary>

- A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03, torch 2.13.0+cu129, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1.
- Unit test: main (1388100) with this patch, compiled extensions from the v0.30.0 wheel, run with `--noconftest` because the env lacks `tblib`; the test only uses `monkeypatch`.
- Engine check: v0.30.0 (ced6857) with the same patch. `supported_kv_cache_layouts` and `get_flashinfer_layout_string` are identical on v0.30.0 and main.
- The other five layouts also run in FlashInfer's attention benchmark on A100; LHBNC is the only one that asserts.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, code and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests on my own hardware.

just get error msg early, right?

@vadiklyutiy Yep. FlashInfer can't run LHBNC either way. Right now the layout gets accepted and the engine then dies on that AssertionError during startup, so this just surfaces the error earlier, along with the layouts that do work.
What is the reason to force `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC`?

@vadiklyutiy  Honestly, no production reason. I hit it while experimenting all six layouts via VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT for a layout study. FlashAttention and Triton run LHBNC fine on A100, FlashInfer is the one that crashes. The point is just that FlashInfer shouldn't advertise a layout it can't run. related PR #60005

@vadiklyutiy Yes, both only show up when LHBNC is forced, but they're different bugs. This PR is about FlashInfer. FlashAttention and Triton actually handle LHBNC fine, but FlashInfer just claims it can and then asserts. And #60005 is about the offloading connector. It can't handle LHBNC whichever backend you use, and a connector has no way to reject a layout during resolution, so it silently writes the wrong bytes.

I could also fix both in one place by dropping LHBNC from the default list, but I'm not sure that's the right call, since kernels like FlashAttention and Triton do support it. So I think keeping them as separate fixes is better.

@stecasta Thanks! Done. FlashInfer now gets its set from a small helper, `get_flashinfer_kv_cache_layouts()` in `backends/utils.py`, and the annotation drops `| None`.

Hi @hyunnnchoi, thanks for the contribution.

LGTM. Declaring a set instead of `None` also gives FlashInfer a vote in `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` when it shares a worker with another declaring backend. Against every backend that declares a set at this head (b12x, QSA, the DSv4 indexer, Dots3, kpool tail, sparse MLA SM90, flex/TurboQuant/HPC), the resolved layout comes out the same, so the only behaviour change is the earlier error for LHBNC.

`envs.py` says LHBNC "hoists the head dim outside the block dim; backends must opt in via AttentionBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()", but `_DEFAULT_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE` still lists LHBNC, so every backend that returns `None` gets it without opting in. That gap is the common root of this bug and #60005. If opt-in is the intended contract, dropping LHBNC from the default list and having the backends that do handle it (FlashAttention and Triton, per your A100 runs) declare it would fix both in one place and cover the next backend that returns `None`. If it isn't, the `envs.py` comment is stale. Fine to land this as the FlashInfer-side fix either way, but worth settling which one is intended.

Minor: this is `_DEFAULT_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE` minus LHBNC, written out by hand. Deriving it, e.g. `tuple(l for l in _DEFAULT_LAYOUT_PREFERENCE if l.name in _FLASHINFER_LAYOUT_NAMES)` (or a small public helper in `backends/utils.py`), ties the declared set to the mapping `get_flashinfer_layout_string` asserts on, so the two can't drift. The method also never returns `None` now, so the annotation can drop `| None`.

+    assert KVCacheLayout.LHBNC not in layouts
